verdict.rationale: iTerm2 documents two first-party scripting interfaces. A Python package lets scripts control the app and extend its behavior, and 'sophisticated AppleScript support' lets stand-alone scripts launch the app and open sessions in new tabs or windows. A community user independently confirms the Python API 'lets you touch pretty much everything'. missing for 10: explicit evidence of sending text to sessions and querying terminal state, and evidence of a dedicated shell CLI rather than script-based IPC.

support.subject: As a developer, I can script and control the terminal from the command line — open windows, send text, query state — via a documented CLI or IPC interface

citations.quote: iTerm2 offers a Python package which makes it easy to write Python scripts that control iTerm2 and extend its behavior.
iTerm2 has sophisticated AppleScript support allowing one to write stand-alone scripts to launch the application and open multiple sessions with profiles into either new tabs or new windows.
Python Scripting API - Full automation and customization via Python.
Python scripting API: basically AppleScript for iTerm except it lets you touch pretty much everything and it's not soul-crushing to write.
